Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the ShopSphere Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question and answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask a question following the presentation. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome to ShopSphere's Q3 earnings call. Joining me today are Jamie Chen, CEO; Taylor Brooks, CFO; Jordan Lee, COO; Riley Patel, CMO; and Morgan Kim, CTO.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements, including our expectations for future financial performance, business strategies, and market trends. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete list of these risks and uncertainties.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jamie Chen, CEO of ShopSphere.

Jamie Chen:
Thank you, Alex, and good afternoon, everyone. We are pleased to report a strong Q3 performance, driven by robust GMV expansion, accelerating seller services adoption, and proactive preparations for the holiday peak. We saw significant growth in active buyers and orders, with marketplace momentum underscoring our competitive positioning.

Our focus remains on enhancing seller value-added services and navigating macroeconomic pressures effectively. We are also excited about the initial traction we are seeing with our updated fee structures, which have spurred seller onboarding and inventory diversification.

We are investing heavily in supply chain resilience and AI-driven demand forecasting to support seasonal demand.

We are focused on improving customer acquisition efficiency amid competitive marketing dynamics.

Finally, we are committed to leveraging technology for personalized experiences and operational scalability.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Taylor Brooks, our CFO, to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Taylor Brooks:
Thank you, Jamie. Our Q3 revenue was $5.8 billion, an increase of 26% year-over-year. Gross margin was 41.2%, driven by higher-margin value-added services mix and fulfillment efficiencies. Operating expenses were $2.1 billion, representing 36% of revenue. Our marketing investments yielded strong returns, with customer acquisition costs trending favorably.

Our net income for the quarter was $850 million, or $1.42 per share. We ended the quarter with $4.2 billion in cash and cash equivalents. We are raising our full-year guidance to reflect this momentum.

Before moving to operations, let me provide deeper context on several key areas shaping our results. Starting with gross merchandise value, or GMV, the headline metric for our marketplace. For Q3, we delivered $32.1 billion in GMV, exceeding our prior guidance range of 20-23% year-over-year growth and 6-8% quarter-over-quarter. We achieved 27% YoY growth—that's well above last year's Q3 of $25.3 billion—and 12% QoQ from Q2's $28.6 billion. This beat reflects the strength of our ecosystem.

Breaking it down, active buyers expanded 18% YoY to 152 million, propelled by our rewards program and targeted social campaigns aimed at younger demographics in high-growth categories. Orders per buyer rose 6% to 4.3, thanks to AI-powered recommendations handling 68% of sessions and lifting conversions. Average order value increased 3% to $152, supported by bundling in electronics and home categories.

Regionally, North America at 54% of GMV hit $17.3 billion, up 29% YoY, with rapid delivery options in key cities countering competitors. Europe contributed $8.0 billion, 24% growth, strong in core markets despite some softness. APAC delivered $4.8 billion, 31% up, led by emerging market ramps. Supply chain optimizations like AI routing reduced lead times, enabling faster turns and adding incremental lift through dynamic pricing.

This performance highlights our resilience, and we're now guiding full-year GMV to 24-27% growth, with Q4 at the upper end assuming solid holidays.

Shifting to macroeconomic influences, while we've posted resilient numbers—Q3 GMV up 27% and revenue growing 26%—broader pressures have tempered the pace from prior highs. Inflation around 3.2-3.8% has squeezed discretionary spending, which is 68% of our GMV in areas like apparel and tech. We observed AOV declines in these segments, prompting shifts to value options, similar to industry patterns.

Interest rates have curbed big-ticket buys, contracting those categories and reducing BNPL usage. Supply disruptions added freight costs, with regional variances: North America held firm on essentials growth, EMEA faced energy-related caution, APAC shone with rebounds, and LATAM dealt with currency swings.

We've countered with AI personalization lifting AOV, expanded fulfillment networks cutting costs, seller programs for alternatives, and ad optimizations. This positions us for FY24 GMV of $78-82 billion and revenue $14.5-15.5 billion, with potential upside from rate relief.

Next, seller services and value-added services, a high-margin powerhouse delivering $1.1 billion this quarter—up 32% YoY and 26% of total revenue. This segment bolstered EBITDA margins to 19.5%, up 250 basis points.

Seller services hit $550 million, 25% growth on 17% more active sellers at 3.0 million, with take rates at 11.5%. Value-added services exploded to $550 million, 38% up: advertising $260 million, fulfillment $170 million, payments $75 million, and tools $45 million, with 58% gross margins.

Adoption reached 71% of sellers using VAS, up sharply: ads at 45%, fulfillment 34%, payments 27%. Trends include efficiency focus amid demand softness, with smaller sellers boosting ARPU 22%. North America led, Europe advanced despite regs, APAC surged.

Tech like our AI Seller Hub improved forecasts, cutting stockouts, alongside APIs and logistics upgrades passing savings via tiers. VAS now drives disproportionate profitability, guiding 28-33% growth for the year, targeting 78% adoption.

On marketplace fee updates from early Q3, we cut referral fees 140 basis points to 12.9% blended, added tiers for high-volume sellers to 10.5%, reduced storage 28%, and launched flex programs. This spurred 30% YoY new seller adds, 45,500 net new, with activation to 80%. SKUs up 21% QoQ, listings per seller rose.

Pricing adjusted dynamically, ad spend up 28%, fulfillment shifts optimized costs. North America boomed, APAC strong, Europe adapting. Tools like Fee Optimizer boosted GMV per seller 18%. This fuels supply growth, projecting $4.5 billion Q4 GMV add, offsetting take rate dip with volume.

Turning to holiday preparations, defining Q4 from Black Friday through returns, historically 37% of annual GMV. Inventory ended Q3 at $2.9 billion, 20% YoY up, 13% QoQ, at 112% of last holiday peaks per AI forecasts. Electronics $880 million up 24%, apparel $680 million 17%, home $570 million 22%. Turnover 8.4x, safety stocks buffered disruptions.

Demand models project Q4 GMV $13.0-13.8 billion, 25-31% YoY, beating industry 16%. Tailwinds: resilient spending, mobile at 62%, repeat AOV $148. Cyber Five $4.3 billion, Christmas $4.0 billion. U.S. 61%, Europe 24%, APAC 15%. Initiatives: DemandSense AI at 93% accuracy, BOPIS 13%, dual-sourcing, blockchain. Capex $160 million for automation.

Risks managed with stress tests, targeting 39-41% margins and share gains.

Finally, customer acquisition cost—or CAC—was $39.50, down 9% QoQ and 20% YoY, below peers. ROAS 5.1x, CLV:CAC 3.9:1, payback 4.5 months. Marketing at 13.8% of revenue.

Channels: search 6.5x, social 4.3x, affiliates 8.0x. North America $46, Europe $35, APAC/LATAM $26. AI DSP allocates dynamically, zero-party data enhances. Retention shift lowers effective CAC.

These elements drive our outperformance. Now I'll turn it over to Jordan to discuss operations.

Jordan Lee:
Thanks, Taylor. Operationally, we focused on fulfillment scalability and supply chain agility. Our shipping times improved by 28% to average 1.8 days. Fulfillment costs declined 12% per unit. We are implementing advanced robotics in 15 new centers, boosting throughput 32%.

Now I'll turn it over to Riley.

Riley Patel:
Thanks, Jordan. From a marketing perspective, we saw strong results from performance search campaigns and social shoppable content. Customer acquisition costs were $39.50 as Taylor noted. Our brand awareness increased by 24%. We are focusing on retention via loyalty personalization.

Now I'll turn it over to Morgan.

Morgan Kim:
Thanks, Riley. On the technology front, we've been focused on AI recommendation engines and cloud infrastructure. Our website uptime was 99.98%. Mobile app usage increased by 26%. We're investing in edge computing for faster global loads.

Operator, we are now ready for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from Sarah Johnson with Goldman Sachs.

Sarah Johnson:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Taylor, could you expand on the holiday inventory buildup and how you're mitigating supply risks?

Taylor Brooks:
Sure, Sarah. As I detailed, we're at $2.9 billion inventory, strategically allocated with electronics leading. Models project strong demand, and we've buffered with 95th percentile safety stocks, dual-sourcing 72% of key vendors, and blockchain for traceability. Red Sea issues are covered via alternative routes—confident in execution.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Thompson with JPMorgan.

Mike Thompson:
Great, thanks. On seller services, how sustainable is the VAS adoption acceleration, especially with fee cuts?

Taylor Brooks:
Mike, adoption at 71% is sticky, driven by ROI like 4.5x on ads. Fee updates complement by drawing more sellers, who then layer VAS—ARPU up 22%. Tech like Seller Hub locks them in. Expect 28-33% growth sustained.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Morgan Stanley.

Lisa Chen:
Thanks. Jordan or Taylor, macro headwinds seem persistent—how did they specifically hit operations this quarter?

Jordan Lee:
Lisa, Taylor covered the GMV drag from inflation and rates well—about 4-5 points overall. Operationally, we shifted to essentials, expanded hubs to cut costs 15%, and used predictive AI to minimize stockouts by 26%. Resilient setup.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Ruiz with Barclays.

David Ruiz:
Appreciate it. Riley, on marketing ROI, what's driving the CAC drop, and outlook into holidays?

Riley Patel:
David, efficiency from AI DSP real-time bidding, better social creatives, and retention focus—ROAS now 5.1x. Holidays will leverage performance ramps, targeting sub-$38 CAC with seasonal lifts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Wong with Citi.

Emily Wong:
Thanks, team. Morgan, how are tech investments tying into seller behavior post-fee changes?

Morgan Kim:
Emily, our Fee Optimizer and APIs have 58% adoption, simulating scenarios to boost listings 21%. Integrates with ERPs, cutting latency—directly fueling the 30% seller growth Taylor mentioned.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I would now like to turn the call back over to Jamie Chen for closing remarks.

Jamie Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute our strategy and deliver long-term value for our shareholders. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
